allowlist._comment: Allowlist for a2kit Rego policies. Each entry needs a non-empty 'reason'. See docs/dev/rego-toolchain.md.

body_dup.reason: coincidental shape: both implement 'exception kind → transport-specific code, with class-attribute override', but kind maps + override attribute + default value all differ by transport. Extracting a shared helper would save ~2 LOC per site at the cost of a premature abstraction (only 2 transports today, no anticipated 3rd). `http_status_for` was renamed from `_http_status_for` and promoted to public (substrate-side) in `dispatch-pipeline-parity-on-http` (2026-05-27) when it moved from `packages/http/build.py` into `packages/http/_error_render_stage.py`. Revisit if a REST/gRPC adapter lands.

name_collision.reason: functools.wraps-style closure inside decorator factories; convergent name is the Python idiom
decorator-factory inner names; one per substrate-front-door package (http/api.py, mcp/surface.py) — S7 (DecoratorSurface lift) tracked separately
App and AppRuntime each hold a resolver handle; ADR-0019 accepts the mirrored read-side surface
click-group root commands; convergent name across cli/builder.py and di/container.py (latter is unrelated DI concept)
stderr-context and null-context share emit signature by Protocol contract; intentional

back-compat aliases for the canonical `is_basemodel` in packages/formatter/inference.py (R7 resolved). cli/builder.py and codemode/marshal.py import as `_is_basemodel` to preserve call-site readability — the underscore signals 'internal to this module', the implementation is shared

coincidental: app.py._register_router composes a router's DI/state into the App at build time (L5); cli/builder.py._register_router builds the Click/Typer command subtree for a router (CLI surface). Unrelated concerns in different layers — a shared module would couple app composition to the CLI.

coincidental generic verb: connections/cli.py._resolve resolves a saved connection by name; log/emission.py._resolve resolves structured log-field values for a record. Wholly unrelated concepts in unrelated packages.
